correctness.rationale: Reconstructed covariance equality E[X−p|T]=aT, a=σ²/(σ²+v), from orthogonal projection and Cauchy-Schwarz, with mandatory saturation of budget. Bounded conditional Bernoulli expectation forces T and centered noise bounded, hence entire characteristic functions. The identity (1−a)φX′φY=aφXφY′ and a simple complex zero of Bernoulli φX force an integer zero multiplicity m=(1−a)/a=v/σ²; integrating logarithmic derivatives with φX(0)=φY(0)=1 gives φY=φX^m. Conversely exchangeability with m Bernoulli summands yields E[X|S]=S/(m+1), exactly attaining covariance bound. At v=0 constant noise is the only equality. Huang existence of minimizers is essential to promote nonattainment to strict infimum at noninteger v. The 54 finite rational examples test only construction, not the analytic argument.

value.rationale: Provides a mathematically sharp arithmetic boundary for a recognized least-favorable-noise optimization problem, classifying every noise that saturates a universal covariance bound and explaining why integer convolutions cannot interpolate to fractional budget ratios. This nontrivial structural rigidity is independently worthwhile.

final_claim: For independent finite-variance additive noise on a Bernoulli(p) signal, the covariance lower bound Lp(v)≥σ⁴/(σ²+v) is attained exactly when v/σ² is a nonnegative integer; equality noises are exactly shifted Bin(m,p), and all noninteger budgets have strict inequality.
limitations: No exact optimization curve between integer variance budgets.
Published minimizer-existence theorem is a necessary imported premise; finite tests are not infinite proof.
